extracted.intended_audience: STTR grant reviewers, institutional biosafety officers, and collaborating researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional biosafety, select-agent handling, personnel/access control, inventory, waste/decontamination, regulatory registration, and multiple PD/PI leadership/IP terms as required and described in an STTR Phase II proposal involving BSL-3 select agent research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access control to BSL-3
rubrics_metrics.description: Card-key access along with a pass-code is needed to enter the BSL-3; all entries and exits are logged in real-time. Card key access to suite 314G is given to Select Agent approved employees only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No casual traffic is allowed; only approved employees are allowed entrance into that area; no employee may use his/her card-key to give access to an unapproved employee, family member, or any other non-approved persons. “Piggy-backing,” the practice of two or more employees (even if approved for access to the BSL3 area) entering upon use of a single card-key, is not permitted. Each person must individually use his or her card to enter the area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visitor policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No visitors are permitted into the laboratory unless accompanied by a Select Agent approved laboratory employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine maintenance and janitorial services are carried out during customary working hours of the laboratory to limit non-essential presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video surveillance and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Eight video surveillance cameras are mounted and in use to monitor the BSL-3 area. These are monitored at a central campus location, and can be accessed for investigation if tampering with, or removal of agents is suspected or detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Video surveillance of the area is in place to detect any violations of access and safety policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical security of select agent storage
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the Select Agents are stored in a -80°C freezer within suite 314G. The select agent freezer within 314G is secured with a combination lock, thus limiting access to only those persons previously designated as approved persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to the BSL3 laboratory and freezer is allowed only to select agent approved laboratory employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agent inventory logging
rubrics_metrics.description: B. pseudomallei and all Select Agent possession will be monitored in the form of inventory log sheet documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information to be recorded on the Select Agent freezer inventory log includes: user name, agent, date and time removed from freezer, date and time returned to freezer, purpose of use, and date and method of disposal. The inventory list is kept locked in the BSL-3 laboratory, accessible only to approved microbiologists. A quarterly inventory is made of all Select Agents in storage to determine if documentation of amounts in storage are correct. Destruction/disposal of the Select Agents is documented on a log sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work location and containment for viable agent work
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with viable B. pseudomallei will take place in the BSL-3/PC3 suites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any open cultures will be handled within a biosafety cabinet within the BSL3/PC3 suites; Biosafety Class II cabinets are used, with HEPA filtration of single pass hood air to the outside; in addition the BSL3 is under negative pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety cabinet and engineering controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Biosafety Class II cabinets are used, with HEPA filtration of single pass hood air to the outside; in addition the BSL3 is under negative pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open cultures are to be handled inside biosafety cabinets to minimize aerosol exposure and environmental release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal protective equipment (PPE)
rubrics_metrics.description: All personnel working with open cultures of B. pseudomallei will be required to where appropriate PPE including a powered air-purifying respirator (PAPR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every reasonable precaution is taken to ensure that these organisms are handled safely in an environment designed to minimize the risk to laboratory personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decontamination and sterilization after sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: All materials to be discarded will be autoclaved at the end of every work session and the sterilization verified. Other reusable equipment will be decontaminated at the end of every work session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Destruction/disposal of the Select Agents is documented on a log sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory approvals and registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration at the Menzies School of Health Research is through the Biosafety Committee and Laboratory Safety Committee (AQIS registration/Australian Standard AS2243). BSL3 laboratory registration is by The Office of the Gene Technology Regulator (OGTR). Menzies has select agent approval in the United States of America (USA) from the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases/NIH to work in collaboration with the select agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select agent work is subject to approval from the Biosafety Committee and Laboratory Safety Committee and conforms with applicable national regulations and standards (e.g., AS2243, OGTR, NIH/CDC select agent regulations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with transport/shipping rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Menzies conforms with IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations and they are subject to rulings of the Office of the Gene Technology Regulator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimen transport and international transfers must follow IATA and national rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample tracking system and specimen handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Freezerworks, the sample tracking system complying with international conference on harmonization-good clinical practice (ICH-GCP), is used for storage and tracking all specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens (including clinical isolates) will be transferred to the BSL3 laboratory under appropriate containment using high level biosafety standards and tracked using Freezerworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated equipment for select agent work
rubrics_metrics.description: Two biosafety cabinets are dedicated to B.pseudomallei work. One -80 freezer is dedicated to select agents including B. pseudomallei. This freezer is locked and access is given to authorized personnel only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segregation/dedication of equipment and locked storage reduces cross-contamination and unauthorized access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory site design considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no outside facing windows and the BSL3 is located on the third floor of the CMM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Location and facility design (e.g., no outside-facing windows, floor placement) are used to enhance containment and security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel authorization per statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Card key access to suite 314G is given to Select Agent approved employees only (as defined in the Public Health Security and Bioterrorism Preparedness and Response Act of 2002 [42 CFR]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only personnel who meet statutory approval criteria may be designated as approved persons for select agent access.

rubrics_metrics.name: No casual traffic and controlled maintenance schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: All routine maintenance and janitorial services are carried out during customary working hours of the laboratory. No casual traffic is allowed in the BSL-3 laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling non-research activities during controlled times reduces risk and unauthorized exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and verification of sterilization
rubrics_metrics.description: All materials to be discarded will be autoclaved at the end of every work session and the sterilization verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification records should be maintained to demonstrate effective sterilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR performance-of-work and management requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed STIR project will be conducted jointly by the small business concern and the research institution in which not less than 40 percent of the work will be performed by the small business concern and not less than 30 percent of the work will be performed by the research institution; the small business concern will be the primary party that will exercise management direction and control of the performance of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project planning, budgets, and subawards must reflect these minimum percentage allocations and management roles to comply with STTR rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PD/PI roles and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Both investigators will contribute to all aspects of the project; however, each investigator has a distinct role in making the final decisions on scientific direction. The Contact PD/PI is responsible for communication with NIH, assembling application materials, and coordinating progress reports. The other PD/PI will oversee production of the 4C4 mAb, direct evaluation and quality control of monoclonal antibodies, direct quantification studies, and guide BSL3 testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define distinct but complementary responsibilities; both PIs should document decision-making authority and how scientific direction decisions are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership communication and conflict resolution plan
rubrics_metrics.description: To enhance communication among the team the InBios and the AuCoin laboratory will arrange a conference call every two weeks and monthly conference calls or other forms of communication (Skype) with collaborators. In-person visits twice per year for one-day meetings to review data and plan future experiments. Conflicts that are particularly difficult to resolve will be decided by consensus of the PD/PI’s and collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular scheduled communication and predefined resolution pathways help prevent and resolve collaboration disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial management and subaward arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: The PD/PIs will both have access to project funds through separate accounts. A subaward will be issued from InBios to the AuCoin laboratory. The small business will make the budget decisions for InBios while the university PI will make the budget decisions for UNR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant financial arrangements should be clearly allocated in subaward agreements and institutional budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property ownership and licensing terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The Company shall own all right, title and interest in all inventions and improvements conceived or reduced to practice by the Company in the performance of the research. The University shall own all right, title and interest in all inventions and improvements conceived or reduced to practice by University or University personnel. University grants to Company an option for an exclusive license; the rights to said option shall expire three months after University has provided written notice to Company of any such invention. Upon execution of the option the parties will meet within thirty (30) days to begin negotiating the terms of the license. If a license is not executed within three (3) months from the exercise of the option, or the option is not exercised within the Option Period, the University shall be free to license the Invention to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint inventions will be owned jointly and exclusive rights negotiated in good faith; inventorship determined under U.S. patent law. License terms to be reasonable in relation to licenses in the field and industry.
